comments.author: @MyPlanetUnseen
comments.text: The ecological transition on Mount Ventoux is fascinating. It visually demonstrates how high elevation, sheer winds, and exposed limestone prevent topsoil accumulation, creating a localized desert high above the lush oak forests.

replies.author: @EXPLOREHORIZONS66
replies.text: That’s a brilliant observation; the stark contrast in those ecosystems is exactly what makes that landscape so surreal!

comments.author: @HunaTravel
comments.text: These mountain passes are breathtaking, but every sharp turn and sheer drop looks absolutely terrifying. The skill and courage required to drive through them are unbelievable! 🏔😨

replies.author: @EXPLOREHORIZONS66
replies.text: Absolutely. These mountain passes are stunning, but they demand serious skill, focus, and respect from anyone who drives them.

comments.author: @intounseenworld
comments.text: What matters most on a dangerous mountain pass: driving skill, weather, the vehicle, or simply knowing when to turn back?

replies.author: @EXPLOREHORIZONS66
replies.text: All of them matter, but knowing when to turn back is probably the most important. Skill, weather, and the vehicle help — but good judgment keeps you alive.

comments.author: @Aventurex-686
comments.text: These mountain passes make me appreciate highways with guardrails a whole lot more. Every curve feels like nature asking, "How confident are you today?" Meanwhile, I still slow down when I see a sharp turn in my neighborhood. Which mountain pass would you actually dare to drive?

comments.author: @unchartedplanettv
comments.text: Which legendary mountain pass from this video would test your nerves the most: the unpaved cliff drops of Sani Pass or the alternating tunnel turns of San Boldo Pass?
